title: Understanding Soil pH for Healthy Crops
summary: Learn why soil pH matters and how to correct it for better yields.
content: Soil pH measures acidity or alkalinity on a scale of 0 to 14. Most crops grow best at pH 6.0 to 7.5. Acidic soils (below 5.5) reduce nutrient availability; alkaline soils (above 8.5) cause micronutrient deficiencies. Apply lime to raise pH of acidic soils and gypsum or sulphur to lower pH of alkaline soils. Always test soil before applying amendments.
sources: ICAR Indian Institute of Soil Science; state soil testing labs.

title: Drip Irrigation: Save Water, Grow More
summary: Drip irrigation delivers water directly to roots, saving 30-60% water.
content: Drip irrigation uses perforated tubes and emitters to deliver water directly to the root zone, reducing evaporation and weed growth. It is ideal for vegetables, fruits, and sugarcane. Subsidies up to 55% are available under PMKSY. Combine drip with fertigation for best results.
sources: PMKSY guidelines; ICAR Central Institute of Agricultural Engineering.

title: Balanced Fertilizer Use: NPK Basics
summary: Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium are the primary macronutrients crops need.
content: Nitrogen (N) promotes leaf and stem growth, Phosphorus (P) supports root and flower development, and Potassium (K) improves disease resistance and fruit quality. Apply based on soil test recommendations. Split nitrogen into 2-3 doses to reduce losses. Use organic manure along with chemical fertilizers for balanced nutrition.
sources: ICAR fertilizer recommendation handbook; state agriculture universities.

title: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) in Crops
summary: IPM combines biological, cultural, and chemical methods to control pests responsibly.
content: Integrated Pest Management integrates biological control (predators, parasitoids), cultural practices (crop rotation, resistant varieties), and judicious chemical use. Monitor pests regularly with light/pheromone traps. Apply pesticides only when pest populations cross economic threshold levels. Always follow label instructions and pre-harvest intervals.
sources: National Institute of Plant Health Management; ICAR IPM package.

title: Organic Farming: Getting Started
summary: Transition to organic farming with composting, green manure, and natural inputs.
content: Organic farming avoids synthetic fertilizers and pesticides. Build soil fertility with compost, vermicompost, green manure (e.g., dhaincha, sunhemp), and biofertilizers. Use neem oil, trichoderma, and bacillus thuringiensis for pest control. A 2-3 year transition period is typical. Certification requires third-party verification.
sources: NPOP standards; National Centre of Organic and Natural Farming.

title: Cattle Vaccination Schedule
summary: Protect your cattle with timely vaccinations against major diseases.
content: Vaccinate cattle against Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) every 6 months, Hemorrhagic Septicemia (HS) and Black Quarter (BQ) annually before monsoon, and Brucellosis once for female calves aged 4-8 months. Maintain vaccination records. Consult a veterinarian for a herd-specific schedule.
sources: ICAR Indian Veterinary Research Institute; state animal husbandry departments.

title: Poultry Layer Management Basics
summary: Key practices for healthy, productive layer flocks.
content: Provide 16-18 hours of light per day for layers. Maintain 18-22°C temperature and good ventilation. Feed layer mash with 16-18% protein and 3.5-4% calcium. Vaccinate against Newcastle (Ranikhet), Gumboro, and Fowl Pox. Monitor egg production daily; a sudden drop signals health or environment issues.
sources: ICAR Directorate of Poultry Research; state veterinary universities.

title: Fish Pond Water Quality Management
summary: Maintain pH, oxygen, and temperature for healthy fish growth.
content: Ideal pond water pH is 6.5-9.0; dissolved oxygen should exceed 5 mg/L; temperature 25-32°C for tropical species. Monitor morning and evening. Use lime to correct low pH and aerators or water exchange when oxygen drops. Avoid overfeeding to prevent ammonia build-up.
sources: ICAR Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture.
